entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: So, this is where one prays to the gods[n]in your world?

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: The peaceful atmosphere here is[n]the antithesis of a prison cell...

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Hmm? Is that man standing there one of[n]the gods?
Sure is.
He's a priest.
He's a person.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: ...No, that's definitely a human. I don't[n]sense any exceptional abilities from him.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Any more thoughtless answers like that[n]and we'll execute you here and now.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Oh, so a servant to the gods? That explains[n]why I don't sense any exceptional abilities[n]in him.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Yeah, you may be right. At least, I can't[n]sense any exceptional abilities from him.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: If that is the case, then perhaps he's[n]some sort of servant to the gods.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: What is that over there... A smaller room?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: I know! It's an "iron maiden" for reforming[n]criminals, right? Whoever goes inside and[n]fails rehabilitation gets skewered!
It's a confession booth.
Yep—skewered alive.
I have no idea.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Confession... booth?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: You mean, THIS tiny box is where[n]the crimes are confessed?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: I thought so. I felt a sense of foreboding[n]from it.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: No, Caroline. That's the place where you[n]speak with a human to divulge your past[n]misdeeds.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: I believe it is called a "confession booth"...

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Hey! One more smart remark like that[n]and you're getting baton-jabbed, Inmate!

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Caroline. That's the place where you[n]can speak with a human and divulge[n]your past misdeeds.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: I believe it is called a "confession booth"...

entries.speaker: Priest
entries.en: Is something the matter?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Hey, you. We're here for the confession[n]booth deal you have going here.

entries.speaker: Priest
entries.en: Ohhh... You seek to confess? At such a[n]young age?

entries.speaker: Priest
entries.en: All right, which of you would like to[n]go first?

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Which of us? Do you intend to split us up[n]and pick us off one by one?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Hmph, no such luck. We're both going in.

entries.speaker: Priest
entries.en: Erm, I see...

entries.speaker: Priest
entries.en: You're free to do so, but there really isn't[n]much room inside...

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: ...Are you attempting some sort of[n]deceptive practice by calling yourself[n]a servant of the gods?

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: ...You what? Listen to people's concerns?[n]This isn't a form of rehabilitation?

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: ...Regardless, such talk is cheap, but pays[n]quite well.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: We shall undertake this confession[n]and ascertain the truth for ourselves.

entries.speaker: Priest
entries.en: Then, ah, as for your confession...

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Hmmmm, what to confess...

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: It's probably unkind to kick the Inmate,[n]but it's part of my duties as warden,[n]so that can't be held against me...

entries.speaker: Priest
entries.en: "Inmate"? "Warden"?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: This is none of your business. We're[n]speaking to the gods right now.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Recently, I've been shifting my more[n]mundane bookkeeping responsibilities[n]onto Caroline...

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: You WHAT!? I knew my workload was[n]feeling larger for some reason!

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: But... she made so many mistakes in her[n]work that I regret not doing it myself...

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Of COURSE I'd make mistakes when[n]I have nearly twice the work!

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: ...How about yourself, Caroline? Don't you[n]have anything you'd like to confess while[n]we're here?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Uhhh, huh? Like... what?

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: I know you went out and ate menchi katsu[n]all by yourself. Did you really think you[n]could escape my notice?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Erk! I... was curious about the line! Like,[n]what could humans want so badly that[n]they would stand in place for so long—

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Megidolao—

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Fine, fine, fine! I'm sorry! I won't do it[n]again! ...Confession time is over![n]We're done here!

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Odd as it may be, I actually feel quite[n]refreshed.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Were it not for this opportunity, we would[n]have likely kept these matters locked away[n]deep in our hearts.
Have you righted your wrongs?
Did you learn to be kinder to others?
What kinds of sins are you guilty of?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: That's YOUR job, Inmate!

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Know your place.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Why would we do such a thing? I don't[n]see anyone here to whom we owe any[n]kindness.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Did you think we'd actually regret[n]the treatment we've given you so far?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Shut up, Inmate!

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Perhaps your rehabilitation would be[n]better attained with a torture chamber[n]rather than a confession booth.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: By the way, why do humans pray to gods?[n]Shouldn't they be spending that time[n]trying to solve their problems themselves?
Humans have their limitations.
It's a kind of support.
Sometimes it's all you can do.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Yes, I do suppose that is accurate.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: But your rehabilitation shall be[n]carried out by your own strength.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Have you given up on taking care of[n]your own issues?

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Perhaps you're the one who needs the[n]change of heart.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Well, isn't that all too convenient for[n]the humans...

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: I'll bet the gods don't appreciate that[n]answer any more than we do.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: No matter. We've come to learn how[n]these places of worship work firsthand.[n]We'll consider the assignment complete.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Here is your reward.

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: You know, confessions seem like they'd[n]be rather useful to your rehabilitation.[n]You ought to confess to us every day!

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Put that out of mind, Caroline. Once we[n]return, you're going to tell me all about[n]your experience eating you-know-what...

entries.speaker: Caroline
entries.en: Wha—!? But I've already confessed!

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Not enough, you haven't.

entries.speaker: Justine
entries.en: Take us back now, Inmate.
I escorted the twins back[n]to the Velvet Room...
